narrative.intro: Federal contract obligations in New Hampshire totaled $1.4B in FY2026 to date. The state recorded 3,298 awards with an average award size of $433K, and obligations fell 51.0% year over year. The Department of Defense accounted for the bulk of spending with $1.2B in obligations. BAE SYSTEMS INFORMATION AND ELECTRONIC SYSTEMS INTEGRATION INC. received $628M and SIG SAUER INC. received $285M, making those two vendors the largest recipients. Small Arms, Ordnance, and Ordnance Accessories Manufacturing led industry spending with $286M, followed by Other Aircraft Parts and Auxiliary Equipment Manufacturing with $225M and Search, Detection, Navigation, Guidance, Aeronautical, and Nautical System and Instrument Manufacturing with $166M. Annual obligations were $2.9B in FY25 and $2.9B in FY24, and FY26 is a partial fiscal-year total. Other notable agencies with obligations in FY2026 to date include the Department of Transportation with $31M and the Department of Veterans Affairs with $26.5M.

sections.heading: How concentrated is federal buying in New Hampshire?
sections.body: The Department of Defense is the largest buyer with $1.2B in obligations in FY2026 to date. The next-largest buying agencies are the Department of Transportation with $31M and the Department of Veterans Affairs with $26.5M. BAE SYSTEMS INFORMATION AND ELECTRONIC SYSTEMS INTEGRATION INC. and SIG SAUER INC. are the top vendors with $628M and $285M respectively. The top three NAICS categories are $286M, $225M, and $166M, reflecting industry concentration among the leaders.

sections.heading: What changed in FY2026 compared with prior years?
sections.body: Obligations fell 51.0% year over year into FY2026 to date, with a partial-year total of $1.4B compared with $2.9B in FY25. Annual obligations were $2.9B in FY24 and FY25, and they were $1.8B in FY21, $1.7B in FY22, and $1.9B in FY23. The FY2026 to date picture shows much lower overall obligations so far in the fiscal year.

faq.q: How much federal contract money goes to New Hampshire?
faq.a: The state received $1.4B in federal contract obligations in FY2026 to date. Award count totaled 3,298 and the average award size was $433K; the current-year total is a partial fiscal amount.

faq.q: Which agencies award the most contracts in New Hampshire?
faq.a: The Department of Defense awards the most contracts in New Hampshire, with $1.2B in obligations in FY2026 to date. The next-largest agencies by obligations are the Department of Transportation with $31M and the Department of Veterans Affairs with $26.5M.

faq.q: Who are the largest federal contractors in New Hampshire?
faq.a: BAE SYSTEMS INFORMATION AND ELECTRONIC SYSTEMS INTEGRATION INC. and SIG SAUER INC. are the largest federal contractors in New Hampshire, receiving $628M and $285M respectively in FY2026 to date. Other top vendors include ENVISION TECHNOLOGY, LLC with $68.9M and BAE SYSTEMS INFORMATION & ELECTRONIC SYSTEMS INTEGRATION INC with $43.2M.
